pr_title: [WIP] drivers: clock_control: initial support for GD32
pr_body:
This PR (WIP) adds a new clock control driver for GD32 SoCs. It has been briefly tested on GD32F450I-EVAL board for now.

TODO:

- [ ] Port remaining drivers (uart, pwm, dac...)
- [ ] Generalize driver to support more series (VF103, F403, F350, etc.)
- [ ] Add tests

Fixes #49074

cc: @cameled @soburi
pr_comments:
@gmarull 
GD32VF103 support patch post to https://github.com/teslabs/zephyr/pull/1.

Collected some gd32 clock config, may help for the generalization work. 
 
Some pattern for PLL clock IRC source:
  ```
  If IRC16M available:
      use IRC16M;
  If IRC8M available but IRC48M not available:
      use IRC8M;
  If IRC8M and IRC48M both available:
      use IRC48M;
 ```
| SoC | IRC8M | IRC16M | IRC48M |
| ---------- |  ---  |  ---  |  ---  |
|  GD32F4xx  |   -   |  Yes  |  Yes  |
|  GD32F403  |  Yes  |   -   |  Yes  |
|  GD32F3x0  |  Yes  |   -   |  Yes  |
|  GD32VF103 |  Yes  |   -   |   -   |
|  GD32E50x  |  Yes  |   -   |  Yes  |
|  GD32E23x  |  Yes  |   -   |   -   |
|  GD32E10x  |  Yes  |   -   |  Yes  |
|  GD32F1x0  |  Yes  |   -   |   -   |


> ``-`` means not available on this soc.

Note:
  1. GD32F3x0 and GD32E23x series have a dedicated ADC clock IRC28M.
  2. GD32F1x0 series have a dedicated ADC clock IRC14M (GD32F130 and GD32F150) or IRC28M (GD32F170 and GD32F190).

Refer:
 1. [GD32F4xx_User_Manual_Rev2.5](http://gd32mcu.com/data/documents/yingyongbiji/GD32F4xx_User_Manual_Rev2.5.pdf)
 2. [GD32F403_User_Manual_Rev2.5](http://gd32mcu.com/data/documents/yingyongbiji/GD32F403_User_Manual_Rev2.5.pdf)
 3. [GD32F3x0_User_Manual_Rev2.5](http://gd32mcu.com/data/documents/yingyongbiji/GD32F3x0_User_Manual_Rev2.5.pdf)
 4. [GD32VF103_User_Manual_Rev1.3](http://gd32mcu.com/data/documents/yingyongbiji/GD32VF103_User_Manual_Rev1.3.pdf)
 5. [GD32E50x_User_Manual_Rev1.4](http://gd32mcu.com/data/documents/yingyongbiji/GD32E50x_User_Manual_Rev1.4.pdf)
 6. [GD32E23x_User_Manual_Rev1.4](http://gd32mcu.com/data/documents/yingyongbiji/GD32E23x_User_Manual_Rev1.4.pdf)
 7. [GD32E10x_User_Manual_Rev1.6](http://gd32mcu.com/data/documents/yingyongbiji/GD32E10x_User_Manual_Rev1.6.pdf)
 8. [GD32F1x0_User_Manual_Rev3.5](http://gd32mcu.com/data/documents/yingyongbiji/GD32F1x0_User_Manual_Rev3.5.pdf)

issue_context.title: GD32: Use clocks instead rcu-periph-clock property
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
The `rcu-periph-clock` property is not well align with devicetree and should be replaced. The correct property for that use is `clocks`.
This is a step closer to have a full clock capability on the GD32 SoCs family. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Replace `rcu-periph-clock` property by correct `clocks` property. The change itself not require a implementation of clock driver to allow the fix.

**Additional context**
The solution can mimics the following [implementation](https://elixir.bootlin.com/linux/v5.19/source/Documentation/devicetree/bindings/spi/atmel,quadspi.yaml#L85) from Linux. A reference from `&rcu` node + `RCU_TYPE_PERIPHERAL` + clock identificator. The change to correct the property not seems to represent a high effort in the first look.

CC: @gmarull @cameled @soburi

review_comments:
I think it is a need to wait for clock stable here. 
(Or we can change this function as async_on to make compliant the API spec, but we have no method to know stabilized the clocks asynchronously... :-( )
